scope: M1-5 mapping inventory: baseline data nodes x collected fields x emitted paths

interfaces.type.note: platform interface kind → iana-if-type identity (ethernetCsmacd, ieee8023adLag, l3ipvlan, softwareLoopback)

interfaces.admin_status.note: shutdown is the configured state (RFC 8343 enabled); admin-status needs the if-mib feature and with it a mandatory if-index

interfaces.raw_name.note: CLI abbreviation (Et0/1) of the full name; presentation evidence only

ip.vrf.note: RFC 8529: interface bound to the named VRF, plus /ietf-network-instance:network-instances/network-instance[name] with vrf-root; 'default' (global table) is no NI entry

arp.type.note: dynamic/static → origin dynamic/static; interface-own entries → other

arp.age_s.note: RFC 8344 neighbor has no age or expiry leaf

mac.mac.note: list key also needs database-id; not shown by the CLI

mac.port.note: port-ref is the bridge port number; the CLI gives the interface name and no port number

vlan_members.status.note: VLAN active/suspended has no IEEE 802.1Q YANG leaf

trunk.ports[].l2_mode.note: trunk/access is not a leaf in 802.1Q; it is the port's tagged/untagged membership

trunk.ports[].encapsulation.note: 802.1Q tagging on a customer bridge port → c-vlan-bridge-port

trunk.ports[].trunk_vlans.note: allowed list → membership of each VLAN

trunk.ports[].forwarding_vlans.note: VLANs whose spanning-tree instance forwards on the port; needs the VLAN→MSTI map and per-MSTI port state

switchport.ports[].admin_mode.note: Cisco DTP administrative mode (dynamic auto/desirable); no IEEE/IETF node

switchport.ports[].oper_mode.note: DTP negotiation result; bundle membership goes to the LAG model

switchport.ports[].admin_native_tagged.note: native VLAN tagged = port absent from untagged-ports of the PVID VLAN

switchport.ports[].lag_parent.note: placeholder until the LAG model check below; see lag.members

lag.members.note: network view (RFC 8944); the device view is IEEE 802.1AX aggregation-port

lag.bundled.note: bundled = collecting/distributing; aggport's mandatory key-group-name reference is not observed, so it is not exported

lag.member_flags.note: IOS member flags (P bundled, s suspended, D down, I stand-alone, H hot-standby); used by the L2 forwarding analysis

lldp.local_if.note: port list key also needs dest-mac-address (agent); nearest-bridge is assumed only with evidence

lldp.remote_chassis_id.note: remote-systems-data keys time-mark and remote-index are not collected

lldp_local.management_addresses.note: IEEE 802.1AB keeps local management addresses per transmitting port (port keys name + dest-mac-address), as hex octets with address-subtype

lldp_local.vendor.note: the element's mfg-name comes from the identified platform vendor

lldp_local.serial.note: belongs to a chassis component whose component-id is not collected

routes.metric.note: only OSPF routes have a metric node (RFC 9129); static/BGP metrics have none in RFC 8349

routes.next_hops[].vrf.note: next hop resolved in another instance (route leaking)

routes.vrf.note: each NI holds its own RIB under its schema mount (RFC 8529/8528)

ospf_process.processes[].process_id.note: the OSPF process ID the device shows names its RFC 8349 instance (type ietf-ospf:ospfv2)

ospf_process.processes[].vrf.note: the NI whose routing tree holds the instance; an instance spread over several NIs is not exported

ospf_process.interfaces[].ifname.note: references the interface list; the interface is copied into the same tree

ospf_process.interfaces[].area.note: IOS area numbers become dotted-quad area IDs

ospf_interfaces.area.note: IOS area numbers become dotted-quad area IDs

ospf_interfaces.address.note: binds the OSPF row to its interface when the platform shows no name

ospf_neighbors.neighbor_router_id.note: an OSPF router ID, scoped to the routing domain; never a device identity

ospf_neighbors.role.note: the neighbour's DR/BDR role; needs the DR election view of the interface, not exported

ospf_neighbors.dead_time.note: remaining seconds at the observation time; a countdown snapshot, not exported

ospf_neighbors.priority.note: RFC 9129 keeps priority as interface configuration, not per neighbour state

bgp_peers.local_as.note: also names the RFC 8349 instance (type ietf-bgp:bgp): the CLI identifies its one BGP process by the AS

bgp_peers.peers[].state.note: a prefix count in the State/PfxRcd column means established

bgp_peers.peers[].up_down.note: observation time minus the established duration; not exported

bgp_peers.peers[].prefixes_received.note: in the afi-safi the command shows (IPv4 unicast); not exported

bgp_peers.peers[].state_detail.note: platform qualifier of the state, e.g. Idle (Admin)

version.os_version.note: per-image revisions below are used when present

version.virtual_cpus.note: with virtio NICs: ne-virtual (IVY software extension)

version.unix_processor.note: IOS running as a Linux process (IOL): ne-software

version.serial.note: belongs to a chassis component whose component-id is not observed; IOL also prints one

stp.instance.note: rapid-PVST/PVST keep one tree per VLAN; IEEE 802.1Q YANG holds one port state per bridge (ieee802-dot1q-rstp-bridge) or per MSTI, so per-VLAN state is evidence for the L2 forwarding analysis
